Croagh Patrick.title: Croagh Patrick
Croagh Patrick.summary: Croagh Patrick is an isolated 764 m mountain on the southern shore of Clew Bay, west of Westport. The guide describes north, south and west approaches, with a substantial hike to launch and XC potential towards the Sheffries. Strong Atlantic influence can make conditions difficult to judge before reaching the hill and can keep cloud base lower than farther inland.
Croagh Patrick.takeoff:
North: walk from the main northern car park to the shoulder at point A and choose a suitable launch in that area. With a NW component, flying too far into the bowl can encounter turbulence.

South: approach the same shoulder area from the Mountain Rescue station side, following a partly boggy track. This starts higher and can be a shorter walk than the northern approach.

West: approach between the western flank, Ben Goram, and the smaller hill, Cuillean. The hike reaches a small, steep launch area at point B. Confident launch technique is needed. Points A and B identify launch areas rather than surveyed launch pads.
Croagh Patrick.landing:
North: the guide describes slope landing above and south of the car park and fields north of the road. It specifically identifies landowner problems with the field immediately east of the field containing the Ship monument; do not infer landing permission from an apparently open field.

South: there are open landing possibilities, but landing too far east of the main peak can lead to a difficult walk through forest.

West: landing options are described near the road used for parking. No precise landing coordinates are supplied.
Croagh Patrick.toplanding: The guide does not identify a dedicated top-landing site or provide top-landing coordinates. Its northern slope-landing description should not be treated as a confirmed summit landing area.
Croagh Patrick.access:
North: use the main car park on the northern side and hike to the shoulder.

South: take the road towards the Mountain Rescue station and continue on the track; the first part can be wet and boggy.

West: follow the road between Ben Goram and Cuillean, park where permitted and make the steep walk to the western launch area.
Croagh Patrick.parking: The guide supplies northern car park C, a small southern parking area D and roadside western parking E. The northern car park has a time limit according to the source; longer visits require an appropriate alternative. Check current parking arrangements and keep access clear.
Croagh Patrick.hazards:
Maritime Weather: cloud and wind can change quickly under Atlantic influence, with a lower cloud base than inland.
NW Bowl: turbulence can occur if the wind is off to the northwest and the flight goes too deep into the bowl.
Western Spine: avoid drifting low behind the ridge, where rotor is described.
Western Launch: the launch is small and steep.
Southern Approach: wet, boggy ground and forested landing-out areas can complicate access and recovery.
Croagh Patrick.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: No site-specific ATC arrangements are described in this guide.

Sky Road.title: Sky Road
Sky Road.summary: Sky Road is a coastal soaring site west of Clifden, with views towards Slyne Head. It works primarily in a SW wind. The guide describes a relatively low site, around 100 m above the ground below, which may remain usable when higher inland sites are too windy or in cloud; this does not establish conditions on a particular day.
Sky Road.takeoff: Park in the small roadside car park at point A and reach the launch just over the low wall. The published coordinates refer to the car park, not a separate surveyed take-off. The site takes a fairly consistent SW wind. The ridge towards Clifden offers a possible short out-and-return, but becomes lower and shallower with increasingly limited landing options.
Sky Road.landing: The guide identifies bottom-landing options around point B. Without a lift back, recovery involves a long road walk or a steep climb back up. On a flight east towards Clifden, landing areas become smaller and uneven, with power lines and stone walls. There are no bottom-landing options immediately along the sea line on that route.
Sky Road.toplanding: The guide favours returning to the launch area when suitable, but describes it as small and uneven, with the car park behind and a large pond to avoid. Compression over the ridge can push a pilot back towards the wall or fence.
Sky Road.access: Drive west from Clifden along Sky Road to the small roadside car park at point A. Launch is just beyond the low wall. Bottom-landing recovery should be planned before flying because the return on foot is long or steep.
Sky Road.parking: Small roadside car park A at 53.500679, -10.096485. The guide provides no separate launch coordinates; the map therefore marks A as parking.
Sky Road.hazards:
Compression: wind over the top can push a pilot towards or over the wall and fence.
Top Landing: uneven ground, a nearby car park and a large pond constrain the landing.
Clifden Ridge Run: the ridge quickly loses height, with limited uneven landing options, power lines and stone walls.
Sea Line: do not assume a beach or bottom landing is available below the coastal route.
Sky Road.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: No site-specific ATC arrangements are described in this guide.

Maumturks.title: Maumturks - Inagh Valley
Maumturks.summary: The Maumturks form the northeastern side of the Inagh Valley in Connemara, opposite the Twelve Bens. This guide describes launching from Binn Chaonaigh via the Maumean trail, with soaring along steep, rocky peaks and XC potential towards the Sheffries and Maumtrasna. It is a description of this launch area, not a guide to every summit in the range.
Maumturks.takeoff: From the Maumean trail car park, follow the path to the saddle between Binnmore and Binn Chaonaigh, then turn left up the hillside. Look for a suitable flatter area about halfway up. The source marks the launch coordinates as approximate. The contents table describes WSW-SSW wind. Once established above the ridge, the guide describes a run of about 5 km towards Letterbreckaun; a more southerly wind may favour the slope around Binnmore.
Maumturks.landing: The guide describes bottom-landing options along the valley but supplies no specific landing coordinates. Assess the selected field and access rather than treating the whole valley as an approved landing area.
Maumturks.toplanding: Top landing is described near launch, but the ground is rocky, rough and broken by ledges. The guide does not supply a dedicated top-landing coordinate.
Maumturks.access: Follow the N59 from Galway towards Clifden. About 11.8 km after Maam Cross, take the signed turn for the Maumean Trail car park, approximately 3.6 km along the side road. Continue on foot to the saddle, then turn left towards Binn Chaonaigh and find a suitable launch area.
Maumturks.parking: Use the small car park at the start of the Maumean trail, point A, 53.483924, -9.669807.
Maumturks.hazards:
Rapid Cloud Formation: weather can change quickly and orographic cloud may form below the peaks even though the Twelve Bens provide some shelter from the sea.
Rocky Terrain: steep slopes and ledges complicate launching and top landing.
Lee Turbulence: gain adequate clearance before crossing a ridge or going over the back.
Launch Position: the published point is approximate and identifies an area in which a suitable take-off must be found.
Maumturks.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: No site-specific ATC arrangements are described in this guide.

Achill Island.title: Achill Island
Achill Island.summary: Achill Island has a long free-flying history and a variety of coastal and hill sites reached over the bridge at Achill Sound. This regional guide covers Minaun Heights, Minaun Lower Cliffs, Keel West / Lough Accorrymore, Knockmore and Atlantic Drive. They are separate sites with different aspects and landing options. Keel West is not the existing Keel Bay forecast location.
Achill Island.takeoff:
Minaun Heights: the road reaches the transmitter station at approximately 396 m ASL. The main ridge has NW and SE aspects, with northern spurs offering other options. The west cliffs south of the summit can be flown in W-WNW conditions after a crosswind launch from the NW side by the masts; the guide restricts this route to experienced pilots because there are no bottom-landing options along it.

Minaun Lower Cliffs: from the parking area near the sea, walk up the rising ground towards the cliffs and find a suitable launch. The lower site may be usable when the summit is too windy, but can still push a pilot back up the slope. The supplied coordinates locate parking, not the take-off.

Keel West / Lough Accorrymore: an easterly-facing ridge and bowl on the road towards Keem Beach. Launch from the ridge south of the lough and gain height before moving into the bowl. This is a separate western Achill site.

Knockmore: a SW option, described as higher and smoother than Atlantic Drive, with a longer walk to launch. The printed coordinates repeat Keel West's point and are not used for a Knockmore map marker.

Atlantic Drive: a SW-facing series of rocky outcrops extending for roughly two miles, becoming higher and steeper towards the southeast. The source coordinate is shown as a reference point, not a precise, confirmed launch.
Achill Island.landing:
The general Achill description identifies open peat land and the large Keel beach as bottom-landing possibilities, with each site's actual glide and obstacles assessed separately.

Minaun west cliffs: there are no bottom-landing options along the remote cliff run south of the main hill.

Knockmore and Atlantic Drive: the guide describes landing areas before the road, with the sea beyond it; avoid overshooting.

No precise landing coordinates are supplied for these individual sites.
Achill Island.toplanding: Minaun Heights has several top-landing possibilities around the main hill. Stay clear of the transmitter mast and the power lines beside the road. The guide does not provide dedicated top-landing coordinates for Lower Cliffs, Keel West, Knockmore or Atlantic Drive.
Achill Island.access:
Minaun Heights: the summit road approaches from the southern side of the hill and reaches the transmitter station.

Minaun Lower Cliffs: on the road towards Keel Beach, turn towards the sea at the church, about 2.7 km from Keel, and follow the lane to the parking area. Continue on foot up the rising ground.

Keel West: follow the road towards Keem Beach and walk to the ridge south of Lough Accorrymore.

Knockmore requires a longer uphill walk than Atlantic Drive. The source contains conflicting Knockmore coordinates, so an exact approach point has not been added. Atlantic Drive's coastal outcrops are described along the southeastern side of the island.
Achill Island.parking: The summit road gives access to Minaun Heights. A separate Lower Cliffs parking point is provided at 53.960185, -10.045186. No precise parking coordinates are supplied for Keel West, Knockmore or Atlantic Drive; their launch/reference points should not be treated as parking instructions.
Achill Island.hazards:
Minaun Mast / Power Lines: keep clear when launching or top landing near the transmitter station and summit road.
West Cliffs: crosswind launching and a route without bottom-landing options require particular experience and planning.
Lower Cliffs: compression can blow a pilot too far back up the slope.
Keel West Bowl: avoid being blown over the back while flying the bowl above the lough.
Atlantic Drive / Knockmore: rocky outcrops, increasing ridge height towards the southeast and the sea beyond the landing road constrain options.
Coordinate Uncertainty: Knockmore's printed point duplicates Keel West and has deliberately not been plotted; the Atlantic Drive point is a source reference requiring local verification.
Achill Island.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: No site-specific ATC arrangements are described in this guide.

Rossbeigh.title: Rossbeigh
Rossbeigh.summary: Rossbeigh, also written Rossbehy, is a coastal hill above Glenbeigh with views over Rossbeigh beach and across the inlet towards Inch. The guide describes a long, steep soaring ridge, a summit-side parking and launch area, a lower launch for stronger conditions and bottom landing near the beach. Dune soaring in a westerly is described as a separate nearby option.
Rossbeigh.takeoff: The main take-off is above the beach, in front of the upper parking area, at approximately 255 m ASL. A second launch is described about 50 vertical metres below the top, below the wire, with room to prepare two or three gliders. The guide suggests considering this lower position when wind at the top exceeds about 20 km/h, while assessing conditions independently. No separate coordinates are supplied for the lower launch.
Rossbeigh.landing: The guide identifies the football field east of the road behind the beach as the main landing area, point B, at approximately 1 m ASL. It notes a children's playground near the road. The wider beach and public car park lie nearby; this description does not establish current permission to use a field. The dunes for westerly soaring are around a five-minute walk along the beach from the main landing area.
Rossbeigh.toplanding: The main hill is described as unsuitable for top landing. Plan a bottom landing rather than assuming the broad launch area can be used on return.
Rossbeigh.access: From Killarney, take the N72 west to Killorglin, then the N70 towards Glenbeigh. Continue towards the beach on the R564. The hilltop launch and parking are reached by the access road from the west.
Rossbeigh.parking: The upper parking area is beside the main take-off. There is also a public car park behind the beach near the bottom-landing area. The source gives launch and landing coordinates, but no independent parking coordinates.
Rossbeigh.hazards:
Top Compression: wind at the upper launch can read up to about 10 km/h more than the wind away from the crest according to the guide; assess the whole site rather than relying on one reading.
Lower Launch: the alternative area is below a wire and has limited preparation space.
Bottom Landing: the road, playground, public use of the beach and actual field availability require assessment.
Top Landing: the guide specifically describes the hill as unsuitable for it.
Rossbeigh.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: No site-specific ATC arrangements are described in this guide.

Poland: Ciecień.title: Ciecień
Poland: Ciecień.summary: Western slope above Wiśniowa, between the Stradomka and Krzyworzeka valleys. Published take-off elevation: 820 m ASL; approximately 400 m height difference.
Poland: Ciecień.takeoff: Private clearing with room for a few wings. The published direction fields conflict; matching uses only their common W–WNW sector. Southerly deviations can produce turbulence and sink.
Poland: Ciecień.access: Walk up the green trail from Wiśniowa, approximately 50 minutes. Do not block narrow lanes or park on private land without agreement.
Poland: Ciecień.landing: The main meadow is about 2 km northwest and is hidden from launch. Inspect it before flying; the slope and thermal activity can cause an overshoot. No landing GPS has been imported.
Poland: Ciecień.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: Close to the Kraków/Balice TMA. Check current airspace before flight.

Poland: Szczebel.title: Szczebel
Poland: Szczebel.summary: A private, association-managed clearing above Mszana Dolna. Published take-off elevation: 960 m ASL; around 500 m height difference.
Poland: Szczebel.takeoff: Small clearing, essentially one wing at a time. Matching uses N–NE from the launch instructions; the quick-reference fields also mention E. Obtain a local briefing before relying on the wider directions.
Poland: Szczebel.access: Walk from Glisne pass, approximately 3 km to the summit. The association requests a daily or annual site contribution.
Poland: Szczebel.landing: SPBW describes a new Kasinka Mała meadow from October 2025, between road 968 and the Raba. Confirm it using the source map. Keep sawmill truck access clear and do not drive onto the meadow.
Poland: Szczebel.hazards: Trees and edge-of-sector turbulence. Other meadows near the Luboń trail have power lines.

Poland: Śnieżnica.title: Śnieżnica
Poland: Śnieżnica.summary: North-facing clearing above Kasina Wielka. Published take-off elevation: 980 m ASL, with around 450 m height difference.
Poland: Śnieżnica.takeoff: The source gives inconsistent direction summaries. Matching uses the narrower NNW–NNE sector. Strong wind and crosswind deviations can cause collapses immediately after launch.
Poland: Śnieżnica.access: Approach from the ski station or follow the blue trail from Gruszowiec pass. Near the summit cross, a small path descends to the north-facing clearing.
Poland: Śnieżnica.landing: The usual meadow is roughly 2 km northwest, below the ski-station car park, and is not visible from launch. Wind there may be stronger than expected; inspect it beforehand. No precise landing pin is available.
Poland: Śnieżnica.airtrafficcontrolrestrictions: Close to the Kraków/Balice TMA; check current restrictions.

Poland: Podobin.title: Podobin
Poland: Podobin.summary: Spyrkowa Góra above Podobin, between Niedźwiedź and Mszana Górna. Published take-off elevation: 680 m ASL; around 220 m height difference.
Poland: Podobin.takeoff: Large open summit meadow. Matching uses the preferred S–SW sector rather than the wider possible directions. Southerly conditions require experience and careful observation.
Poland: Podobin.access: Approach from Podobin and follow the stony track then the path beside the fields; about 30–35 minutes on foot. Keep farm machinery and village lanes clear.
Poland: Podobin.landing: The source states there is no agreed bottom landing. Inspect fields, fences and landowner arrangements before launch. Do not treat the absence of a pin as permission to use any meadow.
Poland: Podobin.hazards: Thermal gusts, turbulence and abrupt changes of wind direction in the valley.

Poland: Skrzętla.title: Skrzętla

Poland: Skrzyczne.title: Skrzyczne

Poland: Skrzyczne.landing: Kaimówka is no longer an official landing and is not mapped. BSP recommends Lipowa: Pańskie Pola, northwest of the runway, and the meadow Nad kościołem. Stay clear of runway traffic and inspect both approaches.
Poland: Skrzyczne.hazards: Rotor near the NW launch and trees. Do not land on the east take-off or fly close to pilots preparing there.
